## Summary

It has been cold. Throughout the water column, temperatures were colder than normal, by over 2.5 standard deviations in some places. Chlorophyll concentrations were high in some locations near the surface, but were below normal overall.High levels of surface turbidity were encountered at several inner bay sites, reflecting heavy rainfall during the week of the survey. However near-surface, inner-bay salinities were still close to the seasonal mean, indicating that recent rain runoff had not yet mixed deeper than 1 meter in the water column.

<!-- `{r} dateAN` , -->

## Conditions

Air temperatures leading up to this survey cooler than normal, but within one standard deviation of the long-term mean (@fig-Temp_Airport). After a dry June, mid July was wet, with major precipitation falling between the first and last day of this survey. 

Results are shown for the Kasitsna Bay Lab oceanographic survey conducted on 17, and 22 July 2026 by Jen, Kris and Martin in calm conditions.

## Physical oceanography

### Temperature

Water temperatures during the July survey ranged from a minimum of `{r} tsal$temSalR[1]` °C at station `{r} tsal$stn[1]` (`{r} tsal$depth[1]` m depth), in the inner bay, to a maximum of `{r} tsal$temSalR[2]` °C at station `{r} tsal$stn[2]` (`{r} tsal$depth[2]` m depth) in the inner bay. Strong vertical stratification was observed throughout the bay, with a shallow layer of warmer, fresher surface water over cooler, more saline waters below (@fig-tSections_AB, top-left panel). Stratification was less pronounced in the outer bay. Surface waters were warmer and bottom waters were colder in the inner than in the outer bay. Satellite sea surface temperature data with a cooler pool of 8-9 °C waters in lower Cook Inlet (@fig-SST_GOA).  


<!-- , possibly indicating mixing of deep and surface waters.  -->

<!-- T9 is situated around km 30 of the AlongBay transect, cross-sectioning the inner/outer bay transition zone. Sloping salinity and temperature contour lines showed influx of warmer, more saline water at depth, especially on the south side, and an outflow of colder, fresher water on the surface at the north side of T9 (@fig-tSections_T9). While the entire water column was colder than normal, the strong surface water cold anomalies found near the Spit were likely caused by melting pack ice from Mud Bay (also note the dip in salinity at the same location).  -->

Throughout the bay, and at all depth, waters were colder than normal, in some areas by over 2.5 standard deviations (@fig-tSections, top-right panel, @fig-bottomTemp, @fig-TSprofile_T9). Most of Kachemak Bay was about 1 °C colder than normal. Surface waters  in mid-bay of Homer Spit and in Homer Harbor were near or slightly cooler than normal (@fig-T96tempTS, @fig-SWMP-homerdeep-temp). Deep waters, however, remained substantially colder than normal (one standard deviation and more), a pattern that has persisted since last December (@fig-bottomTemp). Surface waters of the Gulf of Alaska and Bering Sea also remained colder than normal in July 2026, as shown by satellite sea temperature anomaly data, in contrast to the extremely warm conditions in the central North Pacific (@fig-SSTA).

### Salinity

Salinity values during the July survey ranged from `{r} tsal$temSalR[3]` PSU at station `{r} tsal$stn[3]` (`{r} tsal$depth[3]`m depth) in the inner bay to `{r} tsal$temSalR[4]` PSU at station `{r} tsal$stn[4]` (`{r} tsal$depth[4]`m depth) in the outer bay. The water column was strongly stratified, especially in the inner bay, with fresher waters in a 10-20 m surface layer (@fig-tSections). 
<!-- Along the mid-bay transect, the fresher water was deeper on the north than on the south side of the bay, indicative of outflows of inner bay waters freshened by rain and glacial melting (@fig-tSections_T9).  -->
<!-- , as evident from the contour lines switching from vertical to horizontal.  
Comment on fresh cold meltwater off Homer Spit?  XXX
-->

<!-- Along the inner bay, across mid-bay (T9) and into the eastern parts of the outer bay, a thin layer (~10-20 m) of cold, fresh water was seen over warmer, more salty water at depth, indicating that there had been enough freshwater input to maintain vertical stratification despite cold temperatures (@fig-tSections).  -->

Most Kachemak Bay near-surface waters were close to or slightly saltier than normal (@fig-tSections, @fig-TSprofile_T9). We could see the effects of heavy rainfall runoff in the high surface turbidity in the inner bay (@turb). However, since the CTD sensors only start measuring at 1 meter depth and seas were calm, we likely did not capture the freshest inner bay surface water during this survey. At depth, outer bay waters were near the long-term mean and continued to be fresher than normal in the inner bay (@fig-tSections, @fig-TSprofile_T9, @fig-SalDeep). 

<!-- Explanation = ? These patterns are consistent with the prolonged winter cold, with spring increases in freshwater inputs to the bay coming later than normal. -->

![Variability of deep-water salinity at station T9-6 off the Homer Spit, compared to the seasonal  means.](./media/5-SalDeepTS.png){#fig-SalDeep}

### Turbidity

High surface turbidity was encountered at several stations from mid-bay to Bear Cove (@fig-turbid). Inner bay waters were more turbid than outer bay waters, with highest levels found in the thin rain-driven fresher surface layer of the inner bay (@fig-tSections_AB). In contrast, outer bay waters were unusually clear for this time of year. 

![Example of high surface turbidity, illustrated by how little of the CTD cage is visible below the surface. (photo: K. Holderied).](./media-2026-07/IMG_2350.jpeg){#fig-turbid} 


## Biological conditions

### Phytoplankton

Elevated chlorophyll concentrations were found in the upper 20 meters throughout Kachemak Bay, with the highest values near the seaward extent of the fresher surface layer in the outer bay (@fig-tSections_AB). Integrated over the entire water column, chlorophyll concentrations were expected to drop slightly from June to July, but decreased from near the long-term mean in June to almost a full standard deviation below the mean in July (@fig-chlorophyll-sa). Our partners from the Kachemak Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve detected potentially toxic *Pseudo-nitschia spp.* as "present" in most samples, apart from T9-6 in the mid-bay, which was recorded as "bloom" and AlongBay-10, where it was "abundant". Also potentially toxic *Alexandrium spp.* cells were detected as "present" in mid-bay, at the head of the bay, and near the mouth of the bay (Kim Schuster, Kachemak Bay NERR, The Phyto Times, 23 July 2026).

### Wildlife

<!-- Two harbor seals were seen off Bear Cove. About 65 Steller sea lions were seen on Flat Island. Birds of note included a yellow-billed loon off Bear Cove. Common murres and marbled murrelets started to return to the inner bay.  -->

A humpback whale and a pod of seven orcas were in the outer bay (@fig-orca). Sooty shearwaters and fork-tailed storm-petrels were seen in the bay for the first time this year, with small numbers in the outer bay. Other birds of note in the outer bay were a northern fulmar and a horned puffin, and over a hundred red-necked phalaropes. 

![Two of seven orcas in outer Kachemak Bay (photo: M. Renner).](./media-2026-07/191A8812s.jpg){#fig-orca}
